findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics on any I/O failure (missing file, permission denied, truncated content)
findings.failure_mode: untrusted or missing file path aborts the entire program instead of returning a typed IoError
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, LeaseError> and use map_err to convert io::Error into a typed error; never unwrap file I/O

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics on non-numeric or empty second field
findings.failure_mode: malformed CSV input aborts the entire load instead of returning a typed ParseError for the specific record
findings.fix: return Result and use .map_err(|e| ParseError{ record: parts[0].clone(), source: e }) on the parse call

findings.problem: (...) as u16 is a lossy cast from u32; values > 65535 silently truncate
findings.failure_mode: a valid u32 in [65536, 2^32-1] wraps to a wrong u16 value, corrupting data silently without any error signal
findings.fix: use u16::try_from(parsed_u32) and propagate the error via ? or Result; reject out-of-range values as a typed LeaseValue error

findings.problem: parts[0] is accessed with unchecked indexing; if the line has no commas the Vec has length 1 and parts[1] will panic on line 19
findings.failure_mode: malformed line (missing comma or missing second field) panics at parts[1] or silently reads a garbage first field at parts[0]
findings.fix: use parts.get(0) and parts.get(1) and return a typed ParseError on None, or use split_once(',') and handle the missing-separator case

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) is hidden I/O inside a function that also does file I/O; this mixes side effects with parsing logic and makes the function untestable without capturing stdout
findings.failure_mode: the caller cannot suppress logging, the function is not a pure parser, and unit tests must stub stdout or accept console pollution
findings.fix: move all println! into the imperative shell caller; the parsing step should be a pure function that takes &str and yields Record or error

findings.problem: load_leases returns Vec<Record> with no error type; all failure modes are hidden behind panic
findings.failure_mode: consumers have no way to distinguish IoError, ParseError, LeaseValueOutOfRange, or MalformedLine; error handling is impossible
findings.fix: define a LeaseError enum with Io, Parse, ValueOutOfRange, and MalformedLine variants; signature: pub fn load_leases(path: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, LeaseError>

findings.problem: load_leaves mixes file I/O (fs::read_to_string on line 9) with CSV parsing and domain construction (lines 10-22)
findings.failure_mode: the parsing logic cannot be unit-tested in isolation; any change to I/O behavior requires re-testing the parser and vice versa
findings.fix: split into: pub fn load_leases(path: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, LeaseError> that reads the file, and a separate pub fn parse_records(lines: impl Iterator<Item=&str>) -> Result<Vec<Record>, LeaseError> that is pure and testable

findings.problem: println! is a side effect hidden inside an iterator map closure; callers cannot control or suppress it
findings.failure_mode: log injection makes the function non-deterministic with respect to output, breaks test isolation, and prevents use in library contexts
findings.fix: remove println! entirely from the library function; expose a callback or structured log event if the caller wants diagnostics

findings.problem: Vec::with_capacity is not used and no try_reserve is called before collecting split parts
findings.failure_mode: unbounded allocation on adversarial input; a single line with millions of comma-separated fields could OOM
findings.fix: if collecting parts, use try_reserve with a known maximum, or better, use split_once to avoid collecting all parts into a Vec at all

findings.problem: No benchmark module exists; no profiler or allocation evidence for load_leases performance
findings.failure_mode: performance characteristics of CSV parsing at scale are unknown; any optimization claims would be ungrounded
findings.fix: add a criterion or custom benchmark for load_leases with realistic lease-file sizes and report allocation counts

findings.problem: No allocation tracing evidence; the function allocates a String per line (read_to_string), a Vec per line (split parts), and a String per field (trim + to_string)
findings.failure_mode: per-record allocation overhead is unmeasured; for high-throughput lease loading this could be a bottleneck
findings.fix: profile with criterion or heaptrack; consider a zero-copy parser using &str slices and split_once

findings.problem: parts[0].clone() clones a String unnecessarily; the value is not shared
findings.failure_mode: wasted allocation per record; while not a correctness bug, it violates the zero-waste principle
findings.fix: use parts[0].clone() only if ownership transfer is needed; consider returning Cow<'_, str> or restructure to avoid the intermediate Vec entirely

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for load_leases throughput or allocation
no profiler evidence for hot path analysis
no allocation tracking (criterion/heaptrack) for the parsing pipeline
no command evidence for cargo fmt, cargo check, or cargo clippy
no second-ring evidence for any performance or correctness claims
residual_risk: Static review only; no build or test commands were run. The code has 8 BLOCKER violations (unwrap on I/O, unwrap on parse, lossy as cast, unchecked indexing, hidden I/O println!, no typed errors, mixed I/O and parsing in one function, no checked allocation). All must be repaired before the crate can pass Holzman gates. Without building, the findings on syntax and clippy lints are unknown.
